subject.title: Telegram should default to allowlist mode with owner ID

question: Should fresh Telegram setup replace pairing-by-default with token-verified owner capture that writes dmPolicy="allowlist" and allowFrom for the captured owner?
rationale: The code path is clear, but the change alters Telegram first-run trust, setup UX, and default DM authorization behavior, which needs maintainer product/security intent.

options.title: Token-Verified Allowlist Onboarding
options.body: Generate a short setup token, capture only the Telegram sender who sends it, and write allowlist config for fresh setups while preserving explicit pairing configs.

options.title: Keep Pairing Default
options.body: Preserve the current pairing default and rely on warnings, docs, and manual allowlist setup for private bots.

options.title: Fold Into Bootstrap Work
options.body: Let the broader one-line bootstrap or cross-channel auto-flip issue own the user-facing flow while this issue remains the Telegram-specific requirements reference.

recommendation.title: Token-Verified Allowlist Onboarding
recommendation.body: Generate a short setup token, capture only the Telegram sender who sends it, and write allowlist config for fresh setups while preserving explicit pairing configs.

likelyOwner.reason: Recent and repeated Telegram setup/runtime history plus prior discussion make this the best available routing candidate.
